- [`D3-C287`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S07-what-are-quality-updates.md) **SpamBrain**: Google's spam updates page says its automated spam detection systems run constantly, and a notable improvement to them, such as to the AI-based SpamBrain system, is called a spam update and listed with Google's ranking updates.

### Special-case crawlers (`special-case-crawlers`): 4

- [`D1-C329`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) **contractual crawlers**: Apart from contractual crawlers, all of Google's automated crawlers obey robots.txt, which Google treats as the way site owners opt out of its crawling.
- [`D1-C330`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) **contractual crawlers**: The only Google-owned crawlers that do not obey robots.txt are contractual crawlers, which crawl a site whose owner has agreed that Google may crawl it however it likes.
- [`D1-C343`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) **special-case crawlers**: Google's crawler documentation says special-case crawlers serve specific Google products where the crawled site and the product have an agreement about the crawl process, so they may ignore robots.txt rules; AdsBot, for example, ignores the global (*) user agent with the ad publisher's permission.
- [`D1-C138`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) **special-case crawlers**: Google's page on verifying its crawlers says Googlebot and Google's other common crawlers resolve to crawl-*.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-*.geo.googlebot.com host names, special-case crawlers to rate-limited-proxy-*.google.com and user-triggered fetchers to *.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-*.google.com, and it publishes each group's IP ranges as JSON files such as common-crawlers.json and special-crawlers.json.

### Storebot-Google (`storebot-google`): 6

- [`D3-C385`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **Storebot**: Google Shopping uses its own crawler, Storebot (Storebot-Google), instead of Googlebot because it needs fresh product information, prices, availability and shipping details and therefore crawls much more often.
- [`D3-C386`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **Storebot-Google**: Storebot-Google is used to validate merchant feeds: when a feed gives a price, Google double-checks it on the merchant's site.
- [`D3-C387`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **Storebot-Google**: Storebot-Google also does deep crawls, for example of checkout pages, which do not belong in the search index; this is another reason it is kept separate from Googlebot.
- [`D3-C388`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **StoreBot**: Google's Merchant Center help says the StoreBot crawler goes through product detail, cart and checkout pages, can fill in checkout forms, and records price, shipping, availability, coupons and payment methods to verify the data merchants share in Merchant Center.
- [`D3-C389`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **Storebot-Google**: Google's crawler list says robots.txt rules addressed to the Storebot-Google user agent affect all surfaces of Google Shopping, such as the Shopping tab in Google Search.
- [`D3-C390`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **Storebot-Google**: Treat Storebot-Google separately from Googlebot in robots.txt and bot protection: a shop that blocks it on product, cart or checkout paths can undermine Shopping price and availability checks, even when Googlebot is allowed.

### Structured data (`structured-data-concept`): 77

- [`D1-C269`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **structured data**: Author's view: an LLM fix loop that stops when Google's test passes proves only that the JSON-LD is valid, not that its values are true; Google's generative AI content guidance asks for AI-generated structured data to be fact-checked as well as validated.
- [`D1-C315`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **structured data**: Google's AI optimisation guide says structured data is not required for generative AI search and needs no special schema.org markup, and on Day 2 Google said raw schema.org is generally not put into model context (D2-C477); use markup for rich-result eligibility and clear data, not as an AI-visibility lever.
- [`D1-C137`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) **structured data**: Google's Inside Googlebot post warns that bloated inline base64 images, large blocks of inline CSS or JavaScript, or megabytes of menus can push a page's text or structured data past Googlebot's 2MB cutoff, and advises moving heavy CSS and JavaScript to external files and placing meta tags, the title, the canonical and essential structured data high in the HTML.
- [`D1-C413`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S11-lightning-session-c-crawling.md) **structured data**: A community speaker said technical SEO remains the foundation for AI search, with site architecture showing the structure and thematic connections of content and structured data adding clarity, but that a technically sound site is only the beginning.
- [`D2-C012`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) **structured data**: Google's guide to temporarily pausing an online business recommends that a shop expecting to sell again within weeks or months stays online with limited functionality, such as a disabled cart, and updates its Product structured data to show current availability.
- [`D2-C014`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) **structured data**: Keep a product page that is out of stock for a few months live with a 200 status, show its availability on the page and in Product structured data, and offer pre-ordering where possible when users would wait for the product. Redirect it only when users would rather switch to a similar product than wait.
- [`D2-C833`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) **structured data**: Google's sitemap guide says Google uses lastmod only when it is consistently and verifiably accurate, and counts a change to the main content, the structured data or the links of a page as significant, but not a changed copyright date.
- [`D2-C446`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) **structured data**: The 'gold nuggets' that Google's feature extraction step pulls out of a page's HTML are structured data (such as JSON-LD), images and videos.
- [`D2-C450`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) **structured data**: Because Google extracts structured data, images and videos only after deduplication, put markup and media on the URL you want as canonical and keep them identical on its duplicates; markup that exists only on a duplicate that loses canonical selection may never be extracted.
- [`D2-C451`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) **structured data**: Google's general structured data guidelines recommend placing the same structured data on all duplicate pages of the same content, not just on the canonical page.
- [`D2-C454`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data turns the loosely structured web into structured information that powers visual search features such as review stars and recipe filters (for example by preparation time).
- [`D2-C456`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data can bring more qualified traffic, because the site can be shown in new, more interesting ways to more people, who are then more likely to click.
- [`D2-C457`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Inside Google, views on structured data split into two camps: one says it is useless because models can generate it or read the page directly, the other says it is the future of machines talking to each other through MCP servers and new standards; the speaker said the truth is in the middle.
- [`D2-C458`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google gave four reasons why structured data is still valuable even though models can extract information from pages: precision, extra content, efficiency and focus.
- [`D2-C459`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data gives the high precision that complex schemas such as sale pricing need, with higher accuracy than large-scale extraction by large language models (LLMs).
- [`D2-C462`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's guidance on generative AI content warns that AI output can contain hallucinations and says AI-generated metadata, including structured data and image alt text, should be fact-checked before publishing and the markup validated.
- [`D2-C463`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data often carries non-visible metadata that the page text lacks, such as full ISO dates or stable identifiers for user-generated content.
- [`D2-C467`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's structured data documentation says not to mark up content that is not visible to readers of the page, and not to add structured data about information that users cannot see even if it is accurate.
- [`D2-C468`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: The 'non-visible metadata' argument is not a licence to mark up hidden content, since Google's structured data guidelines still require markup to describe what users can see; use markup for the machine-precise form of facts the page shows, such as a full ISO date with time zone for a visible event date or a homepage url for a named organisation.
- [`D2-C469`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Parsing structured data is significantly cheaper and more efficient than relying on LLMs for every complex extraction task.
- [`D2-C471`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Rule-based parsing of markup is nearly free by comparison with AI models, so Google will always prefer extracting information from structured data over model-based extraction.
- [`D2-C473`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data explicitly points to the pertinent data on a page, which reduces noise and stops Google's systems from pulling in extraneous information such as prices of related products.
- [`D2-C474`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's systems sometimes fail to determine a page's main content correctly, and structured data helps because site owners tend to mark up what is actually important rather than boilerplate or ads.
- [`D2-C476`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: The structured data Google processes is not fed very differently to AI Overviews and AI Mode: after cleaning and quality work, the same data goes to both the classic results page and the AI features.
- [`D2-C480`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's guide to optimizing for generative AI features lists 'overfocusing on structured data' among the things site owners don't need to do: structured data is not required for generative AI search and no special schema.org markup is needed, though it remains worth using because it helps pages become eligible for rich results.
- [`D2-C481`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's developer site has a number of case studies that show traffic and session-duration gains from structured data.
- [`D2-C482`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: A Google case study shown on stage (published May 2018) reported that Rakuten Recipes got 2.7 times more traffic from search engines and a 1.5 times increase in session duration after implementing recipe structured data.
- [`D2-C483`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: The speaker called the Rakuten study old and said the world has changed a lot, but expects the link between structured data and more interactive, visually appealing results to hold for the foreseeable future.
- [`D2-C488`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google will never penalise a site just for having more structured data on its pages than Google uses; extra markup does not hurt.
- [`D2-C489`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Describing every semantic detail of a page in markup is probably not worth the effort; focus on the structured data that Google or other consumers actually use.
- [`D2-C490`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google recommends using the Search gallery in its developer documentation to find the structured data features that suit a site; the gallery shows each feature and how Google uses the markup.
- [`D2-C491`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's structured data types fall roughly into two groups: broad page-level types such as breadcrumbs and article, and vertical-specific types such as recipes, events and products.
- [`D2-C492`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Pick only the structured data types that are relevant to a page instead of adding every type Google is interested in.
- [`D2-C494`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google accepts three structured data syntaxes, JSON-LD, microdata and RDFa, which are all valid and are extracted at the very start into the same pipelines, so they are interpreted identically downstream.
- [`D2-C498`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google recommends testing and previewing structured data in the Rich Results Test, which shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid.
- [`D2-C499`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Test structured data manually first and only then put it into the site's templates.
- [`D2-C500`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data that is not relevant to the page's content can be treated as abusive: Google's filters make it ineffective, and egregious cases can lead to a manual action.
- [`D2-C501`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's general structured data guidelines say a structured data manual action removes a page's eligibility for rich results but does not affect how the page ranks in web search.
- [`D2-C502`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Use unique identifiers in structured data, for example the homepage URL in an organisation's url property, so Google can tell which specific entity is meant rather than reading just a name string.
- [`D2-C503`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Several plug-ins emitting the same markup type is one of the most common structured data problems: the duplicates can make an event details page look like a list of events and change how Google interprets the page.
- [`D2-C505`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's shopping structured data launches of the previous year (2025) added support for merchant loyalty programs and shipping policies, letting merchants define a policy at organisation level and specify details at product level.
- [`D2-C506`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's structured data speaker said that in the months before the event Google added support for validity dates on sale prices in product structured data, so merchants no longer need to rush to remove a sale price when the sale ends for fear it shows wrongly in snippets.
- [`D2-C509`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: More shopping structured data news was left for a Day 3 talk by a Google colleague, Alex.
- [`D2-C514`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google announced server-side structured data validation as coming soon: it will publish downloadable validation rules in SHACL on each structured data feature guide, with other kinds of checks to follow.
- [`D2-C517`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: The SHACL rules will not replace Search Console as the canonical place for structured data reports, because some checks use Google's internal libraries and cannot be expressed in SHACL, but they will catch problems such as a missing required field.
- [`D2-C519`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google plans a SHACL rule set for each of its structured data feature types and will release the rule sets gradually once they have been checked.
- [`D2-C521`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **Structured data**: Structured data makes pages eligible to appear as rich results, Google's structured data talk said in its recap.
- [`D2-C522`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google keeps adding structured data features and recommendations but also removes them: in the previous year (2025) it removed several features that brought little benefit and were little used.
- [`D2-C836`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) **structured data**: Google's Event structured data guide says to give a date without a time, such as 2019-08-15, when the start hour is not known, and to include the UTC or GMT offset whenever a time is given.
- [`D2-C551`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) **structured data**: Google strongly suggests describing a video's metadata with JSON-LD structured data, on top of placing the video in an HTML element on the page.
- [`D2-C957`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) **structured data**: A community speaker said the chapters and entities extracted from an interview transcript can then be used to generate metadata and structured data for the published content.
- [`D3-C219`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) **structured data**: Google's Discover documentation says content is automatically eligible for Discover if it is indexed and meets Discover's content policies, needs no special tags or structured data, and is not guaranteed to appear.
- [`D3-C315`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's Visual Elements gallery describes a text result as based on the page's textual content, with attribution, title link and snippet; attribution can include the site name, favicon and visible URL, and a rich result typically relies on structured data.
- [`D3-C324`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Rich results differ from other search features because Google builds them from extra data that site owners provide, usually structured data and usually in JSON-LD format.
- [`D3-C325`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: AI Mode and AI Overviews are not rich results but standard search features: they need no structured data to function and work with the normal text results from Google's index.
- [`D3-C326`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's AI features guide says there are no additional requirements, and no special schema.org structured data, needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown with a snippet.
- [`D3-C327`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google said that if AI Mode one day showcases images, recipes or similar elements, those parts would need structured data, but in their current form AI Mode and AI Overviews require pretty much nothing extra.
- [`D3-C328`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Day 2 said the structured data Google processes also feeds AI Overviews and AI Mode (D2-C476), while Day 3 said these features do not need structured data to function: markup is not a condition for appearing in AI features, but data taken from it can still reach them.
- [`D3-C329`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's structured data feature guide lists the kinds of structured data Google supports with a search feature and what each can do to a site's search results.
- [`D3-C330`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Article structured data is a broad type with many properties and nested types, which Google uses to learn more about published content, such as its headline, author and publication date.
- [`D3-C331`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's rich results slide said Article structured data is not required to appear in Top Stories but is highly recommended for all articles.
- [`D3-C333`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's Article rich results slide said structured data can be used to indicate that content is behind a paywall.
- [`D3-C336`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's site name documentation says site names are generated automatically from a site's home page and references to it on the web, and that a site can indicate its preferred name with WebSite structured data on its home page.
- [`D3-C337`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Review structured data lets a site specify how its users rated something; the review snippet shows an average star rating and often the number of reviews of a product, service or piece of content.
- [`D3-C343`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google Search displays product rich results from product structured data; it may also use the product data a merchant provides in Google Merchant Center, but Merchant Center is not required for them.
- [`D3-C344`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Google's Product structured data introduction says that providing both on-page structured data and a Merchant Center feed maximizes eligibility for shopping experiences and helps Google understand and verify the data; product snippets may take pricing from the feed when the markup lacks it.
- [`D3-C345`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Product annotations on Google Images results also come from product structured data and do not need Google Merchant Center.
- [`D3-C346`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: To appear in the Shopping tab of Google Search, a product must be submitted in Google Merchant Center; product structured data alone is not enough.
- [`D3-C349`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Product structured data can help Merchant Center in some cases, for example during data validation, but Merchant Center does not require it.
- [`D3-C350`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: Merchant Center's automatic item updates use structured data and other product data found on landing pages to fix price, sale price, availability and condition mismatches in a merchant's product data; Google says they do not replace regular feed updates.
- [`D3-C351`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) **structured data**: For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed.
- [`D3-C354`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **structured data**: Product snippets in Google Search are powered by both shopping feeds and schema.org structured data.
- [`D3-C380`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **structured data**: Most of the new conversational feed attributes were already available in schema.org, so Google ties them back to structured data and can use them from product markup as well as from feeds.
- [`D3-C405`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) **structured data**: Web markup is an efficient and unambiguous way for sites to share product data with Google, Google Shopping said, repeating the Day 2 structured data talk.
- [`D3-C646`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) **structured data**: Google usually picks up structured data updates within hours to one or two weeks, sometimes immediately.
- [`D3-C647`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) **structured data**: Google may never use structured data from a site it does not trust: once it sees markup it does not trust, it does not touch it.
- [`D3-C701`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) **structured data**: Google's closing slide said AI on Google is just SEO: AI features on Google Search use exactly the same processes as traditional results, so no new acronym is needed, as none was for mobile-first indexing or structured data.

### Tokenization (`tokenization-concept`): 9

- [`D1-C039`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) **tokenization**: Gemini is not part of Search, but it uses crawlers for data, shares some technologies such as tokenization and deduping, and grounds on the Search index.
- [`D2-C319`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) **tokenization**: For languages written with spaces between words, such as English and German, Search tokenization splits a sentence into its individual words.
- [`D2-C325`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) **Tokenization**: Tokenization for AI models such as Gemini, in training and in inference, differs from tokenization for Search, although Gary Illyes qualified this with 'or mostly'.
- [`D2-C326`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) **tokenization**: In tokenization for AI models, common English words stay whole and each maps to a numeric token ID, so the model works with IDs rather than with the words; on Google's slide the word 'can' had the same ID, 740, both times it appeared.
- [`D2-C328`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) **tokenization**: Google's two tokenization slides showed the difference on the same sentence: the Search tokenizer kept 'robots.txt' and 'tl;dr' as single tokens, while the AI-model tokenizer split them into pieces such as 'tl' and 'dr' or 'robots' and 'txt', with the punctuation as separate tokens.
- [`D2-C329`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) **tokenization**: Day 1's slide said Gemini shares technologies such as tokenization with Search, while on Day 2 Gary Illyes showed that the two tokenizers split the same text differently ('or mostly'); read this as a shared processing step with different outputs, so Search's word tokens and Gemini's sub-word tokens are not the same units.
- [`D2-C720`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) **tokenization**: Google's Search index stores the tokens produced by tokenizing each page, as they are, together with the metadata attached to the tokens during tokenization.
- [`D3-C108`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S04-lightning-session-k-facets-of-quality.md) **tokenization**: A community speaker compared Googlebot to an inspector who cannot enter the shop and only looks through the window, seeing the page as ones and zeros, which the speaker linked to tokenization.
- [`D3-C109`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S04-lightning-session-k-facets-of-quality.md) **tokenization**: The inspector metaphor blends two steps: Googlebot fetches pages during crawling, while tokenization happens later when the page is processed for the index, as Google explained on Day 2.

### Trending now (`trending-now`): 7

- [`D2-C760`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Google Trends has two flagship experiences: the Explore page and Trending now.
- [`D2-C765`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Trending now, a tab at the top of Google Trends, shows the topics people are searching for on Google right now.
- [`D2-C766`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Google said Trends' Trending now covered 125 countries at the time of the talk (October 2026), plus regions within many of those countries.
- [`D2-C767`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Google's August 2024 blog post said Trending now was available in 125 countries, with regional trends in 40 of them; the current Trends Help page says 100+ countries and regions.
- [`D2-C768`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Google's documentation says the Trending now page shows an approximate, bucketed search volume for each trend, with its growth against a predicted baseline.
- [`D2-C804`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: For ideation, Google recommended Google Trends' Trending now, where a real-world event shows up within about ten minutes as people hear the news and search for it.
- [`D2-C805`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Trending now**: Google said journalists use Google Trends' Trending now every morning to find content gaps: topics people are searching for that their publication may need to cover.

### Trends Explore (`trends-explore`): 14

- [`D2-C760`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Explore page**: Google Trends has two flagship experiences: the Explore page and Trending now.
- [`D2-C761`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: The Google Trends Explore page, which Google called the heart of Trends, shows search interest in a query or topic and how it changes over time.
- [`D2-C762`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: Google launched a brand-new Google Trends Explore page at the beginning of 2026.
- [`D2-C763`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: The legacy Google Trends Explore page is still available but will be retired: Google is adding its features to the new Explore page until everyone can move to the new one (no date was given).
- [`D2-C769`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: A Google Trends Explore chart presented on stage put worldwide search interest in Gemini above ChatGPT for the first time ever in September 2025, during a sharp surge for Gemini.
- [`D2-C778`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Explore page**: A Google Trends engineer found the cause of the 2012 'ai' spike by zooming in on that time range on the Explore page and reading the related queries.
- [`D2-C790`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: For keyword selection, Google recommended entering candidate keywords on the Google Trends Explore page, setting the relevant country, region and time frame, and seeing which terms have the higher search interest.
- [`D2-C794`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: The 'Commonly searched queries' section of the new Google Trends Explore page, called related queries in the legacy Explore page, lists queries that people typed in the same search sessions as the entered term.
- [`D2-C798`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: For scheduling, Google recommended checking on the Google Trends Explore page whether the topics relevant to your domain show seasonality; many topics do, though not all.
- [`D2-C806`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: The new Google Trends Explore page has a 'Suggest search terms' button that opens an optional Gemini-based side panel.
- [`D2-C811`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: Quick comparisons, a recent Google Trends Explore page feature, show year-over-year, month-over-month and week-over-week comparisons as chips when a single search term or topic is entered.
- [`D2-C813`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: Google said colour maps of the geographic breakdown of search interest (regions within a country, or countries worldwide) had launched in the new Google Trends Explore page about a month before the October 2026 talk.
- [`D2-C815`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: The category filter of the legacy Google Trends Explore page has been reintroduced in the new Explore page.
- [`D2-C816`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **Google Trends Explore**: Search Engine Roundtable reported on 2 September 2026 that Google had announced category filters for the new Google Trends Explore page, usable with or without a query.

### URL Inspection (`url-inspection`): 12

- [`D1-C140`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) **URL Inspection tool**: Search Console's robots.txt report shows the robots.txt files Google found for the top 20 hosts of a Domain property, with their fetch status, warnings and errors; to test whether a specific URL is blocked, Google's help page points to the URL Inspection tool and to Google's open-source robots.txt library.
- [`D2-C133`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Put everything indexing depends on (title, meta description, canonical, robots meta tag, main text and links) in the raw HTML so it is available without rendering, let JavaScript add enhancements only, and check the rendered HTML in URL Inspection for the rest.
- [`D2-C158`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: When something is missing from a rendered page, check both robots.txt and the Content Security Policy: the URL Inspection live test shows the page resources, the JavaScript console output and a screenshot of the rendered page.
- [`D2-C176`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection tool**: To check whether JavaScript content is affected, open the URL Inspection tool in Search Console or the Rich Results Test and look for that content in the rendered HTML tab.
- [`D2-C178`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Google's URL Inspection help says the tool's live test examines a URL in real time, so its results can differ from Google's indexed version of the page.
- [`D2-C179`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Check rendering per template rather than per URL: inspect one URL of each page type (product, category, article) in URL Inspection and confirm that the main content, prices and internal links appear in the rendered HTML.
- [`D2-C240`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection tool**: Because Web Fragments monkey-patches core browser APIs such as document, history and location, test pages that use it in Google's rendering (the rendered HTML in Search Console's URL Inspection tool or the Rich Results Test), not only in a normal desktop browser.
- [`D2-C250`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Because Google flattens shadow DOM when it renders, content that Web Fragments places in a shadow root can in principle be indexed with the host page, but only if it appears in the rendered HTML; check that in URL Inspection rather than relying on a library's promise of indexability.
- [`D2-C298`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Check robots.txt for Disallow rules covering JavaScript bundles, build folders or API endpoints the page calls while rendering, including on separate API or CDN hostnames with their own robots.txt, then confirm in URL Inspection's live test that the rendered HTML contains the main content.
- [`D2-C308`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) **URL Inspection**: Google's URL Inspection help says a valid live test only confirms that Google can access a page for indexing; the page must still meet other conditions to be indexed, such as having no manual action, not being a duplicate and being of high enough quality.
- [`D2-C404`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) **URL Inspection tool**: A broken canonical setup does not fail visibly: pages still load normally while the choice of URL passes to the search engine's own heuristics, so canonical tags need a regular audit with a crawler and the URL Inspection tool.
- [`D2-C975`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S17-poster-session-h-indexing.md) **URL Inspection tool**: The Day 2 poster topics included technical SEO testing in CI/CD pipelines, internal links that move rankings, Search Console's URL Inspection tool and API, getting everyone on board during complex site migrations, a CMS migration from WordPress to Contentful, the 'global Spanish' problem and going beyond prompts.

### User-triggered fetchers (`user-triggered-fetchers`): 4

- [`D1-C273`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **user-triggered fetchers**: A community speaker pointed out that, according to Google's documentation, user-triggered fetchers, which fetch a page because a user asked for it, generally ignore robots.txt rules.
- [`D1-C138`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) **user-triggered fetchers**: Google's page on verifying its crawlers says Googlebot and Google's other common crawlers resolve to crawl-*.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-*.geo.googlebot.com host names, special-case crawlers to rate-limited-proxy-*.google.com and user-triggered fetchers to *.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-*.google.com, and it publishes each group's IP ranges as JSON files such as common-crawlers.json and special-crawlers.json.
- [`D2-C122`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **user-triggered fetchers**: Google says user-triggered fetchers, which fetch a URL because a user asked for it in a Google product (for example Gemini Notebook fetching URLs users add as sources, or Google-Agent acting on a user's request), generally ignore robots.txt rules.
- [`D2-C123`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) **user-triggered fetcher**: Google documents Gemini grounding only as content from the Search index at prompt time; the live read of a specific page at a user's request, described on stage, is not documented, so it is unclear whether it works like a user-triggered fetcher, which generally ignores robots.txt, or follows Google-Extended.

### WebMCP (`webmcp`): 6

- [`D1-C281`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **WebMCP**: A community speaker presented WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol) as a way for a site to declare the actions it offers to AI agents, for example booking an appointment in a calendar, so an agent does not have to scrape the interface; the speaker called it faster, easier and cheaper.
- [`D1-C282`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **WebMCP**: A community speaker said that at the time of the event (30 September 2026) WebMCP was not supported by all browsers but could be enabled for testing through browser flags.
- [`D1-C283`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **WebMCP**: A community speaker said WebMCP has two kinds of tools: declarative ones, mostly HTML annotations such as the fields of a contact form, and imperative ones for other actions such as booking, filtering a catalogue, adding products to a cart, getting product specs or reordering.
- [`D1-C284`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **WebMCP**: A community speaker summed up agent readiness in three layers: a good CLS improves how agents see content, schema, landmarks and ARIA how they understand it, and WebMCP how they interact with it.
- [`D1-C316`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) **WebMCP**: Chrome's WebMCP documentation describes WebMCP as a proposed web standard that site owners can test through an origin trial starting in Chrome 149 or through a Chrome flag for local development.
- [`D2-C303`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) **WebMCP**: Combining schema-based interfaces with web standards such as WebMCP lets a site expose tools to AI agents, which can then operate the interfaces, for example to test them.

### X-Robots-Tag (`x-robots-tag`): 4

- [`D2-C069`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) **X-Robots-Tag**: Google's robots meta tag specification says robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag headers are found only when a URL is crawled, so the rules on a URL disallowed in robots.txt are never seen and are ignored.
- [`D2-C095`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) **X-Robots-Tag**: Google's Search documentation gives notranslate as a rule for a robots or googlebot meta tag or an X-Robots-Tag header, and says the rule opts a page out of all translation features in Google Search.
- [`D2-C529`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) **X-Robots-Tag**: Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies.
- [`D2-C530`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) **X-Robots-Tag**: Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route.

### YouTube (`youtube`): 18

- [`D1-C148`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) **YouTube**: The keynote's third driver was that information quality remains a core focus for Google, which wants high-quality sources to serve across Google Search, its AI experiences in Search, YouTube and Discover.
- [`D1-C497`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) **YouTube**: Google said YouTube has surpassed Netflix as the number one streaming service, in the US and around the world.
- [`D1-C498`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S01-welcome-and-opening-keynotes.md) **YouTube**: Cite YouTube's lead as US streaming watch time measured by Nielsen: that is the figure YouTube publishes, and no published Google source backs the keynote's 'around the world'.
- [`D1-C125`](../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) **YouTube**: Since 16 September 2026, US publishers and creators qualify for a Search profile with 10,000 followers across YouTube, Instagram, X or TikTok, and media organisations can claim and manage profiles for all their sub-brands from one login.
- [`D2-C547`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) **YouTube**: Gary Illyes said over 219 million people in Southeast Asia consume content on or through YouTube daily (the daily scope was heard in two independent recordings but is not verified).
- [`D2-C928`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) **YouTube**: Gary Illyes suggested considering video hosting platforms such as YouTube or Vimeo, because they solved video search years ago.
- [`D2-C959`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S14-lightning-session-f-media.md) **YouTube**: From one unified interview transcript, a community speaker's workflow produces a full article for the website and shorter angles for LinkedIn, Substack, X and YouTube.
- [`D2-C748`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **YouTube**: Google Trends data covers searches on Google Search, including web, image, shopping and news search, plus searches on YouTube.
- [`D2-C749`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **YouTube**: Google Discover is not included in Google Trends, because Discover is a content feed with no search box, while Trends counts only the queries people type into Google Search or YouTube.
- [`D2-C819`](../40-sessions/day2/D2-S24-google-trends.md) **YouTube**: Google has published a YouTube series of about eight episodes on using Google Trends for research, journalism, marketing and SEO.
- [`D3-C443`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: Platform properties let a user verify ownership of an Instagram, TikTok, X or YouTube account in Search Console and see the traffic Google sends to that account.
- [`D3-C444`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: Google said it is working on adding more platforms to Search Console's platform properties beyond Instagram, TikTok, X and YouTube.
- [`D3-C448`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: The platform property landing page lists the account's top-performing content items, for example a channel's top YouTube videos, and the items trending up and trending down.
- [`D3-C450`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: Because platform properties bring many new users to Search Console, Google published documentation and strategy guidance on them, covering how to identify the Search audience, use the 24-hour real-time view, export data and compare platforms such as Instagram and YouTube.
- [`D3-C451`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: In a YouTube platform property, long-form and short-form videos can be compared in the Performance report's comparison mode by URL pattern, /watch versus /shorts/; Instagram posts (/p/) and reels can be compared the same way.
- [`D3-C452`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: In the example YouTube report shown in Google's Search Console talk, long-form videos still got more traffic and more impressions from Google than Shorts; this was one example channel, not a general finding.
- [`D3-C453`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S12-inside-search-console-what-s-new-how-to-use-it.md) **YouTube**: Media teams that publish on YouTube, Instagram, TikTok or X should add each account as a Search Console platform property and compare formats by URL pattern; Google's July 2026 post says an account already used for a Search profile should already give access to its data.
- [`D3-C590`](../40-sessions/day3/D3-S16-mastering-the-messy-middle.md) **YouTube**: Google's slide advised partnering with category opinion formers, such as YouTube creators, experts and institutions, who can give consumers extra reassurance.
